title.en: Ronnmark R function and companion columns
title.zh: Ronnmark R 函数及伴随列

summary: Evaluate the source's Taylor, asymptotic or integral R-function branch and 2x2 companion matrix.

capability: Ronnmark R function and companion columns

operation: evaluate the Ronnmark R function and companion matrix

discovery.model: Ronnmark rational response for magnetized Maxwellian dispersion
discovery.boundary: branch comparisons and arithmetic follow source real/complex behavior; scalar finite inputs only

identity.relation: dimensionless x and lambda to selected R branch and companion matrix
identity.direction: dimensionless x and lambda to selected R branch and companion matrix
identity.definition: Ordered RYLA selector uses three Taylor tests, an asymptotic test, then a 16-point Gauss-Legendre integral fallback; RC[0,1]=d(lambda R)/d lambda. At exact lambda=0, R=H=x/(x*x-1) and both scaled-x companion derivatives equal -x*(x*x+1)/(x*x-1)**2; rational components are rounded only on output. For nonzero lambda every exact nonzero integer x has a genuine R/H pole. At exact x=0 the paired harmonic responses and both x-scaled derivatives vanish analytically within the selected branch.
identity.model: Ronnmark rational response for magnetized Maxwellian dispersion
identity.coordinates: dimensionless complex x and lambda plane
identity.boundary: branch comparisons and arithmetic follow source real/complex behavior; scalar finite inputs only
assumptions: Input units and normalization follow the declared ports; no physical parameters are inferred.

inputs.name: x
inputs.description: Ronnmark argument Y, equal to (omega-kz*vt*czj)/wcs in the frozen source. Real or complex scalar. Units: dimensionless (normalized frequency). Validity constraint: must be finite (no `NaN`/`inf`); real inputs use real double-precision arithmetic and complex inputs use complex double-precision arithmetic (their rounding differs; see the Behavior and boundaries section); this operator accepts scalars only, so array inputs must be looped elementwise by the caller.
inputs.constraints: Must be finite (no `NaN`/`inf`); real inputs use real double-precision arithmetic and complex inputs use complex double-precision arithmetic (their rounding differs; see the Behavior and boundaries section); this operator accepts scalars only, so array inputs must be looped elementwise by the caller.

inputs.name: lambda_
inputs.description: AL=lambda=(k_perp*rho_c)^2, the Ronnmark expansion parameter (frozen source). Shape/axis order: scalar (real or complex; with a nonzero imaginary part on the complex kx plane). Units: dimensionless. Validity constraint: Must be finite; nonnegative real for real kx and complex for complex kx. Exact lambda=0 selects the Taylor constant term; x=+/-2 is removable, x=+/-1 is a genuine pole, and an unrepresentable full RC raises FloatingPointError.
inputs.constraints: Must be finite; nonnegative real for real kx and complex for complex kx. Exact lambda=0 selects the Taylor constant term; x=+/-2 is removable, x=+/-1 is a genuine pole, and an unrepresentable full RC raises FloatingPointError.

outputs.name: R
outputs.description: R(x,lambda)=RC[0,0], the selected Ronnmark response [dimensionless]. Finite complex; exact lambda=0 uses x/(x*x-1); genuine poles or any unrepresentable required companion raise FloatingPointError.
outputs.constraints: Finite complex. No alternate branch, silent zero or partial response is substituted on numerical failure.

outputs.name: H
outputs.description: RC(1,2) column, the `dRsj` read by the frozen source. Complex scalar. Units: dimensionless. Validity constraint: computed in the same branch as `R`; the source series expansion verifies analytically that this column equals d(lambda*R)/dlambda = R + lambda*dR/dlambda, not dR/dlambda itself (in the frozen source PN_I is proportional to lambda^(I-1) while the accumulation weight is I, so RC(1,2) = R + lambda*dR/dlambda).
outputs.constraints: Computed in the same branch as `R`; the source series expansion verifies analytically that this column equals d(lambda*R)/dlambda = R + lambda*dR/dlambda, not dR/dlambda itself (in the frozen source PN_I is proportional to lambda^(I-1) while the accumulation weight is I, so RC(1,2) = R + lambda*dR/dlambda).

outputs.name: branch
outputs.description: String identifying the branch actually selected; shape/axis order: scalar string (enumeration label, no array axis), one of `'RTAY(AL<4)'`, `'RTAY(|Y|^2>75*AL)'`, `'RTAY(|Y|>40+AL/3)'`, `'RASY'`, `'RINT'`. Units: dimensionless (enumeration label). Validity constraint: one of the five strings, corresponding one-to-one to the frozen source criteria.
outputs.constraints: One of the five strings, corresponding one-to-one to the frozen source criteria.

outputs.name: RC
outputs.description: Full 2x2 complex matrix (complex128, understood in the reference runtime's column-major order). Units: dimensionless. Validity constraint: `RC[0,0]==R` and `RC[0,1]==H`; `RC[1,0]` and `RC[1,1]` are companion columns computed in the same branch and are unused by the frozen source. All four entries must be finite; at lambda=0 the second row is -x*(x*x+1)/(x*x-1)**2 in both columns.
outputs.constraints: `RC[0,0]==R` and `RC[0,1]==H`; `RC[1,0]` and `RC[1,1]` are companion columns computed in the same branch and are unused by the frozen source. All four entries must be finite, even when the caller only needs R.

preconditions: branch comparisons and arithmetic follow source real/complex behavior; scalar finite inputs only
supported: Evaluate the source's Taylor, asymptotic or integral R-function branch and 2x2 companion matrix.
excluded: No mode identity or arbitrary-parameter accuracy is inferred beyond the declared numerical method.

failure_semantics.invalid_input: Raises ValueError for declared invalid inputs; numeric conversion errors may propagate for unsupported Python objects.
failure_semantics.runtime_failure: Raises FloatingPointError for genuine poles or a nonfinite/unrepresentable required R/H/RC component; no alternate branch or partial response is substituted.
failure_semantics.nonconvergence: Not applicable; no iterative root solve is exposed.
failure_semantics.partial_results: No partial mapping is returned after an exception.

example.code:
from scirel.kinetic import evaluate_ronnmark_r
r=evaluate_ronnmark_r(0.5,0.25); assert r['branch']=='RTAY(AL<4)'
example.expected: The asserted result follows the declared output contract.

scope: Independent basis: the contract's own definition R = sum_n n**2 Gamma_n/(lambda(x-n)) and H = d(lambda R)/d lambda = sum_n n**2 Gamma'_n/(x-n), with Gamma_n = exp(-lambda) I_n(lambda), evaluated at 40 mpmath digits using mpmath.besseli.
The reference does not implement a recurrence: a recurrence would reproduce the implementation's own truncation error as well as its value, so agreement would say nothing about the sum.

Test matrix: b = 0.2, 1, 4 and 8 at real and complex x, covering the RTAY and RINT selector branches, with H additionally checked against a 40-digit central difference of R so two independent routes to the derivative must agree.
The reference's own truncation is bounded: the harmonic tail beyond |n| = 80 is measured at 1e-75 to 1e-201 on these points, so the comparison floor belongs to the implementation.

Failure matrix: one assertion per channel -- wrong harmonic weight (R), wrong lambda derivative (H), wrong lambda = 0 limit, an unconverged truncation passed off as converged (tail test), and a pole that should raise returning a series value.
Precision budget, written before measurement: 1e-9 for R and 1e-7 for H on the RTAY branch, 1e-10 and 1e-8 on RINT; measured worst values are 3.7e-10 and 6.9e-9 (RTAY), 7.2e-11 and 2.7e-9 (RINT).
The budget is per branch because the branches truncate differently; a single number would either hide the RTAY floor or be unreachable for RINT.
verification.evidence_ceiling: Bounded to the declared RYLA selector and its five branches at the twelve-sample scale plus the complex-x points the k_perp scan visits. Established by an independent 40-digit harmonic sum computed from mpmath Bessel functions, with the oracle's own truncation measured below 1e-40; measured agreement is 3.7e-10 for R and 6.9e-9 for H. Excluded scope: global tensor accuracy, the dielectric assembly that consumes R, and any claim that these two branches cover every point in the selector's domain.
known_limitations: The quadrature and Taylor truncations set the 1e-9 / 1e-7 floor; the relation would tighten under a bit-golden comparison or an exact rational intermediate, which this evidence does not claim.
Only the RTAY and RINT branches were exercised here; the RASY branch is covered by its existing tests and by the branch-budget entry, not by a measured sample.
